PNP Sensor Wiring and NPN PNP Sensor Difference in One Table

A PNP sensor gives +24 V on its output when it detects a target (sourcing). An NPN sensor connects its output to 0 V when it detects a target (sinking). Use this table when wiring a PNP proximity sensor or an NPN sensor to a PLC.

PointPNP sensorNPN sensor
Output typeSourcing (+24 V)Sinking (0 V)
Load connected betweenOutput (black) and 0 V (blue)+24 V (brown) and output (black)
PLC input cardSinking input, common at 0 VSourcing input, common at +24 V
Output when ON (meter to 0 V)About 24 VAbout 0 V
Common inIndia, EuropeJapan, Asia, older US machines

How to Wire a PNP Proximity Sensor

  1. Brown wire to +24 V DC.
  2. Blue wire to 0 V DC.
  3. Black wire to the PLC input terminal.
  4. PLC input common to 0 V.

If the input LED never turns on, check that the sensor type matches the card: a PNP sensor on a sourcing card, or an NPN sensor on a sinking card, will not switch the input.
